input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: The audit right binding us (Licensee) already meets several playbook points: an independent CPA/audit professional selected by mutual agreement, effectively 30 days' lead time, records-only review with no access to our systems, and Licensor-borne cost unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found (p0064) — better than the 10% fallback. However, the clause places no limit on audit frequency, so Licensor could demand repeated audits; unlimited audits are walk-away territory and fail the fallback's "once per year" requirement on a material term. Our redline adds the once-per-twelve-months cap plus business-hours conduct and a confidentiality-bound auditor, leaving notice and cost allocation untouched.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor, provided that Licensor may request no more than one (1) such audit in any twelve (12) month period, that the audit shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Licensee's operations, and that the auditor shall be bound by written obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those in this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We limited the audit right to one audit per twelve months, during business hours, with the auditor bound by confidentiality, consistent with our playbook position; the existing 30-day notice and Licensor-borne cost (absent a 5% discrepancy) are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Cap audit frequency at once per 12 months, require business hours and a confidentiality-bound auditor.
